rules.text: Make suspend functions safe to call from the main thread: move blocking work, such as disk or network access, off it with `withContext` and a dispatcher passed in to the class. Do not hardcode `Dispatchers.IO`, so tests can swap the dispatcher.
Keep an interrupt handler short and fast, with no waiting: `delay()` does not work inside one and `millis()` stops counting. Declare every variable it shares with the main program `volatile`.
Never write Wi-Fi passwords, API keys or device credentials into source files. Keep them in an untracked file, such as a `secrets.h` listed in `.gitignore`, or pass them in as build flags.
Await tasks. Never block on one with `.Result` or `.Wait()`; make the calling method `async` instead.
Keep nullable reference types on (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`) and fix their warnings. Never silence one with the `!` operator unless the code has already checked the value.
Keep `contextIsolation` and `sandbox` on, and `nodeIntegration` off, in every `BrowserWindow` and webview. Never flip one of them to make a feature work.
In a preload script, expose only named functions through `contextBridge`. Never expose `ipcRenderer` or any other Electron API itself to the page.
In the main process, check the `sender` of every IPC message and validate its arguments before you act on them.

Add or upgrade a library with `npx expo install <package>`, which picks a version known to work with the project's React Native version. After changing dependencies, run `npx expo install --check` and fix what it reports.

If `ios/` and `android/` are listed in `.gitignore`, `npx expo prebuild` generates them from the app config, and the next `npx expo prebuild --clean` erases hand edits. Make native changes in `app.json`, `app.config.*` or a config plugin instead. If the project commits those folders, edit them directly.
Only variables named `EXPO_PUBLIC_...` are built into the app, and anyone can read them from the installed app. Never put a secret, such as a private API key, in one. Keep secrets on a server.
Run `npx expo-doctor` after you change dependencies or the app config, and fix what it reports before you call the step done.
Give variables, parameters and return values static types in GDScript, such as `var speed: float = 200.0` and `func hit(damage: int) -> void:`.
Put movement and physics code in `_physics_process(delta)`, which runs at a fixed rate, not in `_process(delta)`.
Design scenes with no dependencies on where they are placed. A child tells its parent what happened with a signal; it does not reach up or across the tree with long `get_node()` paths.
Run Gradle through the project's wrapper, `./gradlew`, never a `gradle` installed on the machine, so every build uses the Gradle version the project chose.
If the project has `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, declare dependencies and their versions there, and refer to them from build files. Do not write a version inline in a build file.

In the App Router, pages and layouts are Server Components by default. Add `"use client"` only to the component that needs state, event handlers, effects or browser APIs, as far down the tree as you can, never to a whole page or layout.

Only environment variables named `NEXT_PUBLIC_...` reach the browser, and their values are built into the JavaScript bundle. Never give a secret that prefix. Read secrets only in server code, and start each module that reads one with `import 'server-only'`.

Fetch data in Server Components where you can, and pass it down as props. In a Client Component, read a promise passed from the server with `use`, or use the data library the project already has, such as SWR or React Query. Do not write your own fetching in an effect.
Declare libraries in `lib_deps` in `platformio.ini`, each with a version. Build and test with `pio run` and `pio test` for the board you changed, using `-e <environment>`.

Run Python and its tools through the project's environment: `uv run`, the virtual environment's own `python`, or `python -m <tool>`. Never install packages into the system Python with a bare `pip install`.
Declare a dependency in the file the project already uses, `pyproject.toml` or a requirements file, never only in an install command. Ask before adding one (R-CODE-006).
Open text files with an explicit encoding, such as `open(path, encoding="utf-8")`. Python's default encoding depends on the platform and its locale.
Catch the specific exceptions you expect, such as `OSError` or `ValueError`. Never write a bare `except:`, and never catch `Exception` only to pass.
Pass `subprocess` commands as a list of arguments. Never use `shell=True` with text you did not write yourself.
Run tests with the runner the project already uses, `python -m pytest` or `python -m unittest`, from the project root. Name test files `test_*.py`, and keep them where the project keeps its tests.

Call hooks only at the top level of a component or a custom hook: never inside a condition, a loop or a nested function, and never after an early return. Name a custom hook `use` followed by a capital letter, such as `useCart`.
Give each item in a rendered list a `key` that comes from the data, such as an ID. Never use the array index as the key when items can be added, removed or reordered.

Do not use an effect to compute values from props or state, or to respond to a user event. Compute such values during render, and handle events in their handlers. Use effects only to sync with something outside React.
Never change state or props in place. Make a new object or array, such as `{ ...user, name }` or `[...items, item]`, and pass it to the setter.

Handle a small platform difference with `Platform.OS` or `Platform.select`, and a large one with separate `.ios.tsx` and `.android.tsx` files. Check a change on both iOS and Android, or say which one you did not check.
Render a long or growing list with `FlatList` or `SectionList`, which render only the rows on screen. Never render one with `.map()` inside a `ScrollView`.

In library code and in code that handles input, return a `Result` instead of calling `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!`. Keep `unwrap()` for tests and for cases that cannot fail, with a comment that says why.
Before you call a step done, run `cargo clippy` and `cargo test`, and fix the warnings clippy reports.
Update the UI only on the main actor. Mark view models and other UI state `@MainActor`, and never change the UI from a background task.

In app code, never force-unwrap an optional with `!` or call a throwing function with `try!`: either one crashes the app when it fails. Use `if let`, `guard let` or `??`, and `do`/`catch` or `try?`. Tests may force-unwrap.

Before code uses a protected resource, such as the camera, location or contacts, add that resource's purpose string (`NS...UsageDescription`) to `Info.plist`. Without it, access fails and the app may crash.
Grant each window only the permissions it needs, in a capability file under `src-tauri/capabilities/`. Never widen a scope, such as file system access, beyond what the feature uses.
A Tauri command that can fail returns a `Result` whose error the frontend can show; it never panics. Validate every argument that comes from the frontend.
Run the project's type check, its `typecheck` script or `tsc --noEmit`, before you call a step done. Never loosen `tsconfig.json`, such as turning off `strict`, to make errors go away.

Never silence a type error with `any`, `@ts-ignore` or a `!` non-null assertion. Use `unknown` and narrow it, or fix the type. If a suppression is truly needed, use `// @ts-expect-error` with the reason on the same line.

Treat data from outside the program, such as JSON from the network, files, environment variables and user input, as `unknown`, and check its shape before you use it. A type assertion with `as` checks nothing at runtime.

Install packages with the package manager whose lockfile the project has: `package-lock.json` means npm, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pnpm, `yarn.lock` Yarn, and `bun.lock` Bun. Commit the lockfile change with the dependency change, and ask before adding a dependency (R-CODE-006).
Move or rename assets inside the Unity Editor. If you must do it on disk, move or rename the asset's `.meta` file with it: the `.meta` file holds the ID that every reference to the asset uses.
Never search for objects, such as with `GameObject.Find`, in `Update` or other code that runs every frame. Look the reference up once, in `Awake` or `Start`, and keep it in a field.
Apply forces and other `Rigidbody` changes in `FixedUpdate`, not in `Update`, so physics stays the same at any frame rate.
